source.title: Grokfast: Accelerated Grokking by Amplifying Slow Gradients
source.authors: Jaerin Lee; Bong Gyun Kang; Kihoon Kim; Kyoung Mu Lee

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures delayed generalization on grokking tasks and tests whether a different training intervention, low-pass gradient amplification, changes its timing.
record.gate_note: The authors' grokfast experiments and the reported baseline behavior bear on grokking. Related-work claims about mechanisms and results cited from other papers are not recorded as rows. Hyperparameter sweep curves are described as having sweet spots, but values visible only in those plots are not separately extracted.
record.test_reason: This is mainly a methods paper (Grokfast), but its baseline reproduces Power et al.'s setting: a two-layer Transformer on x·y mod 97 with 50% training data. Validation accuracy reaches 0.95 at 39,890 iterations, against training saturation at about 500, roughly a 97× delay. That baseline bears directly on V1. The MNIST baseline with ×8 initialization also shows a delay (44,022 iterations to 95% validation accuracy) and bears on V3. The other rows compare the authors' own method with the baseline and do not test any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that amplifying slow-varying gradient components brings grokking forward by up to ×50 on algorithmic, image, text and graph tasks. They also propose a three-state (initialized, overfitted, generalized) state-transition view, in which Grokfast reaches a generalizing solution nearer to initialization.
record.recipe_differences: The study modifies training by adding a moving-average or EMA-filtered gradient; it does not reproduce the original study's training recipe. It applies the intervention to modular multiplication and selected image, molecule, and text tasks.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports sweet spots for Grokfast gain and filter window/momentum, and reports effects that depend on weight decay. For modular multiplication, the largest reported acceleration for Grokfast-MA occurs at wd = 0.01; the same weight decay without Grokfast makes training unstable.

fits_no_version.finding: Amplifying low-frequency gradient components (Grokfast MA/EMA) cuts the iterations to generalization by ×13.6 to ×50.5 on modular multiplication and ×22 on MNIST. Using only the slow gradients fails to converge. The speed-up is larger combined with weight decay 0.01.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The grokking delay depends on optimizer dynamics: amplifying slow-varying gradient components shortens it.

fits_no_version.finding: Across 5 seeds, baseline runs travel far in parameter space after overfitting (BC distance 563.7±199.4 ×1000) and end at widely varying points. Grokfast runs end much nearer to initialization (AC 35.8 vs 570.7).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Different optimizers and seeds reach different generalizing parameter configurations (parameter space only; algorithms not identified).

record.problems: Main timing and validation outcomes are reported without uncertainty estimates. Some results are conveyed by curves, and the grokfast settings include selected hyperparameters; the study does not sweep training-set size to test the delay-versus-data-size relation.
record.rows_left_out: No separately reported numerical outcomes were omitted. Plot-only values from the Grokfast hyperparameter sweeps in Figures 4, 7, and 8 were not extracted individually.

untested.parts: Whether the delay grows as the training set shrinks; only a 50% training fraction is used.
All of it: no circuit or progress-measure analysis.
Switching the delay on or off via initialization scale or weight norm. Large init is used but not compared with standard init, and QM9/IMDb baseline delays are not quantified.
Efficient-circuit account, critical dataset size, ungrokking.
Algorithm identity across runs. Parameter-space distances differ across seeds, but no algorithm is identified.
No control of adaptive-optimizer instabilities or softmax floating-point limits.

missing.what: MNIST baseline grokking delay: 44,022 iterations to 95% validation accuracy with ×8 Kaiming init; the paper says this setup exhibits grokking.
IMDb LSTM said to exhibit grokking only with larger initial weights; no baseline delay or init comparison is quantified.
Baseline validation loss rises and then falls during the delay (Figure 8b).

record.verdict_notes: This is primarily a method paper. Only the baseline measurements bear on the claim versions. The method-versus-baseline rows were relinked to none and summarized under fits_no_version. The V1 verdict rests on a single baseline run with no uncertainty reported. The V3 verdict rests on text and table values not captured in a baseline row. The paper is not an original source. Preprint.

versions.untested_parts: Does not sweep training-set size, so it does not test whether the delay grows as the training set shrinks.
No circuit formation, memorizing-component removal, or mechanistic progress measure is measured.
Reports grokking-like results on non-algorithmic tasks with selected training setups, but does not systematically switch the behavior on or off by sweeping initialization scale or weight norm.
No LLM pretraining or fine-tuning is studied.
Weight decay is varied in some experiments, but the study does not test the proposed efficient-circuit account, a critical dataset size, or ungrokking below it.
Does not identify or compare algorithms learned across runs.
Does not control for adaptive-optimizer instabilities or floating-point/softmax limits.

relation.reason: Its own baseline training and validation trajectories measure delayed generalization, independently of the acceleration comparisons.

tranche.reason: The study tests delayed generalization using modified optimization with moving-average or EMA gradient amplification. Its algorithmic baseline supplies direct evidence, but using the original task and architecture does not establish reproduction of the original training method; the pack explicitly identifies the recipe as different.

source_check.notes: The MNIST threshold inconsistency should be preserved when citing Table 4. QM9 reports validation-loss curves and minimum losses, without quantified baseline grokking delay or matched switching controls.
